comparison: Perfect agreement on computational efficiency claims (C1, C37, C51-C53). Both evaluations find the speedup claims well-supported, with peer reviewers explicitly citing Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure S2 as compelling evidence, matching OpenEval's assessment of 30-40× speedup validation.

Complete agreement on population structure effects on LD (C2, C3, C41, C44, C46). Both evaluations support these claims, with peer reviewers explicitly acknowledging that 'cross-chromosome LD can be substantial' with implications for population structure studies.

Partial overlap on HLA findings (C4, C5, C55). OpenEval addresses broader set including centromere claims (C6, C7, C60, C65), while peer review focuses on HLA-specific findings (C4, C5, C55, C88). Both find claims supported, with peer reviewers implicitly validating through method validation.

Overlap on centromere findings (C6, C7, C60, C65). OpenEval groups HLA and centromere claims together, while peer review separates them. Both evaluations support the chromosome 11 centromere observations, with peer reviewers noting 'very good agreement' with PLINK validates these findings.

Strong overlap on chromosome length-LD linear relationship (C8, C9, C71). OpenEval includes chromosome 11 exception (C10) and quantitative leave-one-out analysis (C79), while peer review focuses on the core linear relationship. Both find claims supported through method validation.

Perfect agreement on ASW chromosome 8 anomaly (C11, C83, C92). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanistic explanation (C92), while peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED but don't directly address the speculation, focusing on observational validity.

Complete agreement on LD decay analysis (C67-C69, C74-C75). Both evaluations support these claims about population-specific LD patterns, with peer reviewers noting implications for population structure studies.

Minimal overlap on HLA variation claim (C88). OpenEval groups this with chromosome 11 and recombination biology claims (C79, C80), while peer review includes it with HLA findings. Both find it supported.

Minimal overlap on leave-one-out analysis (C79). OpenEval groups this with HLA and recombination claims, while peer review includes it with linear relationship findings. Both support the quantitative validation.

Strong overlap on theoretical foundation (C18, C19). OpenEval includes additional citations (C22, C23), while peer review focuses on core mathematical derivation. Peer reviewer explicitly states 'the method and its derivation are solid.'

Partial overlap on background context (C22, C23). OpenEval groups these with theoretical foundation, while peer review includes them with broader background claims. Both find established literature appropriately cited.

Strong overlap on software implementation (C12, C29, C30). OpenEval includes capacity testing (C20), while peer review focuses on core implementation claims. Both confirm software functionality and availability.
Minimal overlap on capacity testing (C20). OpenEval groups this with software implementation, while peer review includes it with computational limitations. Both support the claim.

Strong overlap on dataset description (C25, C26). OpenEval includes broader background context (C13, C14), while peer review focuses on data quality. Both find data processing appropriately described.

Partial overlap on background context (C13, C14). OpenEval groups these with dataset description, while peer review includes them with broader literature context. Both find background appropriately cited.

Strong overlap on computational limitations (C86, C87). OpenEval includes future directions (C89), while peer review focuses on current limitations. Peer reviewer explicitly confirms the fine-grained resolution limitation.

Agreement on CHM13 prediction (C89) but different evaluation types. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (reasonable speculation), while peer review rates as UNCERTAIN (untested hypothesis). Both acknowledge speculative nature.
Minimal overlap on cited observation (C90). OpenEval treats this as standalone cited claim, while peer review includes it with broader background literature. Both find it appropriately cited.
Minimal overlap on recombination biology (C80). OpenEval groups this with chromosome 11 findings, while peer review includes it with background literature. Both find citation appropriate.
